speaker: narrator
text: Act II: The Gathering Storm

speaker: narrator
text: You left Willowbrook to the sound of the chapel bell, ringing once with no hand on the rope. The mountain path took you up through rock and pine, and from the last ridge you see Greendale: stone houses, more chimneys than you can count, and a white castle above the walls. No banner flies from its highest spire.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira's parting words go with you:

speaker: mira
text: Your road leads to Greendale, Elior. Once there, show the amulet to no one lightly. Those who know what it is will find you.

speaker: narrator
text: The ancient amulet your parents left you lies hidden under your shirt, warm against your chest. Someone came to Willowbrook looking for it, your grandmother said. Keep it hidden.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar, to you, is a word from Willowbrook: a name your neighbours say over bad weather and bad luck, and knock on wood after. A tale to frighten children, and one line in your mother's hand that called him a friend once.

speaker: narrator
text: East of the city the Enchanted Forest begins, a dark line of trees as far as you can see.

speaker: narrator
text: Take a deep breath, and start down the road into Greendale.

speaker: narrator
text: Mountain Path

speaker: narrator
text: A winding trail climbs through rocky terrain between Willowbrook and Greendale. Sturdy trees cast intermittent shade and the path remains well tended despite its remoteness. Glimpses of both settlements appear at overlooks, offering reflective pauses. A small camp site used by travelers rests just off the main trail.

speaker: narrator
text: A small but hardy wildflower that grows along the mountain paths. Its purple petals seem to shimmer slightly in the sunlight, though it appears to have no special properties.

speaker: narrator
text: A sturdy wooden walking stick worn smooth by many travelers. It provides reliable support on mountain paths and could serve as a makeshift weapon if needed.

speaker: narrator
text: There are two fire pits here, not one, and the ashes of one are much older than the other. In the soft ground beside the trail, the same boot prints show twice: one line coming up from Willowbrook, and a fresher line going back down toward it. Hidden under leaves near the fire pit you discover an entry pass to Greendale, dropped, it seems, by whoever left in such a hurry.

speaker: narrator
text: You found an entry pass!

speaker: narrator
text: A mysterious amulet inscribed with runes. At its centre is a worn sigil you cannot place. It is faintly warm in your hand.

speaker: narrator
text: The mountain hermit looks you up and down, the way he might inspect a recruit.

speaker: mountain hermit
text: Greendale, is it? Thirty years I drilled squires in that castle's yard, and I've never heard the city so uneasy. The king gone, the guard half-empty. Walk carefully.

speaker: narrator
text: He unwraps a battered training sword from an old cloth.

speaker: mountain hermit
text: This was Cedric's. I put it in his hands when he was a boy, a squire in that yard. They say he left his post the night the king went, and lost his spurs for it. Take it to him in the castle yard. Tell him the sergeant never believed a word of it.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive a training sword.

speaker: narrator
text: A broad old man in a patched castle cloak, its royal blue faded almost to nothing, sitting straight-backed by a small fire. His hands are scarred across the knuckles, and he watches the path between Willowbrook and Greendale the way a sentry watches a gate.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Mountain Path, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: You think it over. Nothing presses on you just now.

speaker: narrator
text: You rest for a moment, gathering your strength.

speaker: narrator
text: This might come in handy, so you decide to pick it up.

text: New main quest

speaker: narrator
text: The Gathering Storm

speaker: narrator
text: Greendale is bigger than any place you have seen, but the talk in its streets is low and uneasy. People speak of a darkness gathering beyond the walls, and say that if anyone at the castle understands it, it is Sir Cedric.

speaker: narrator
text: The mountain flower is quite pretty, but seems to be just an ordinary wildflower that's adapted to the harsh mountain climate.

speaker: narrator
text: You stop and think over what you know.

speaker: narrator
text: The Gathering Storm: Greendale is bigger than any place you have seen, but the talk in its streets is low and uneasy. People speak of a darkness gathering beyond the walls, and say that if anyone at the castle understands it, it is Sir Cedric.

speaker: narrator
text: You lean on the walking stick, feeling more steady on the rocky path. It's a small comfort and a reliable companion for any journey.

speaker: narrator
text: A well-balanced practice sword with a dulled blade. The grip is worn smooth by years of a young hand, and there is a small notch near the guard. Though not sharp enough for real combat, it's perfect for demonstrating martial skills and training exercises.

speaker: narrator
text: You practice a few sword forms with the training sword. The balance feels good in your hands, and it would be perfect for demonstrating combat skills to someone who needs proof of your abilities.

speaker: narrator
text: The mountain hermit jerks his chin toward Greendale.

speaker: mountain hermit
text: You've still got that blade, I see. Get it to Cedric, and mind you give him my words.

speaker: narrator
text: An official-looking document with the seal of Greendale. The line where the bearer's name should be has been scraped away with a blade, but the seal is whole. It appears to grant passage through the city gates to those who present it to the guards.

speaker: narrator
text: Someone has scraped their name off the entry pass, carefully. The seal looks authentic, and it should allow you passage into Greendale without question.

speaker: narrator
text: Greendale Gates

speaker: narrator
text: A magnificent stone archway marks the entrance to Greendale, the largest settlement you have encountered. Guards in polished mail stand watch, banners fluttering in the mountain breeze. Beyond, cobblestone streets wind between stone houses and bustling shops. The air carries the sounds of commerce—a stark contrast to Willowbrook's quiet charm.

speaker: narrator
text: The Gate Captain looks at your boots, then at your face.

speaker: gate captain
text: State your business in Greendale, traveler. Nobody goes through this gate without a pass.

speaker: narrator
text: An officer of the city watch in polished mail, the watch's badge on his shoulder. He looks at every face that comes up the road, and then at its papers.

speaker: narrator
text: The Gate Captain stands vigilant, watching all who approach. It would be improper to search while he observes you so closely. Perhaps he would relax if you showed him proper papers.

speaker: narrator
text: The Gate Captain turns the pass over in his hands. He runs a thumb along the line where a name should be; it has been scraped away with a blade. Then he looks at the seal, and grunts.

speaker: gate captain
text: Somebody's scraped the name off this. The seal's good, though, and the seal's what I answer for. Welcome to Greendale.

speaker: gate captain
text: A map would help you find your way; the streets in there turn back on themselves. Travelers leave things at the information post by the arch. Have a look before you go in.

speaker: narrator
text: With that, he salutes smartly and walks off along the wall.

speaker: narrator
text: With the Gate Captain gone, you're free to look around. A small information post nearby holds items left by travelers. Among them you discover a detailed city map of Greendale. Someone has drawn on it in grey ink.

speaker: narrator
text: The city map is a professional cartographer's work, showing detailed street layouts, building locations, and district boundaries. Someone has been over it in grey ink, in a small, careful hand. The Silver Stag Inn is circled twice. In the Residential Quarter, at the end of one lane, a cross has been drawn, and beside it a single word: cellar?

speaker: narrator
text: The city map's detailed layout shows the Main Square at the center, with the Market District to the east, Castle Approach to the north, and various other important locations clearly marked. Someone has been over it in grey ink, in a small, careful hand. The Silver Stag Inn is circled twice. In the Residential Quarter, at the end of one lane, a cross has been drawn, and beside it a single word: cellar?

speaker: narrator
text: Main Square

speaker: narrator
text: The heart of Greendale: a great fountain of old heroes fighting beasts, stalls under bright awnings, red roofs all round. The square is crowded, but the talk is low, and it stops when a guard walks past. Castle towers rise to the north.

speaker: narrator
text: Most of the postings on the notice board are mundane announcements about trade regulations and festival dates, but one catches your eye: a call under the Lord Commander's seal for able hands to serve the castle in these uncertain times. Beneath it, in a smaller hand, someone has written: Enquire in the training yard.

speaker: narrator
text: A colorful handbill advertising the Market District's finest merchants and their premium goods. It features a special introduction coupon for new customers seeking quality adventure gear.

speaker: town crier
text: Hear ye, hear ye! Welcome to Greendale, traveler! The Lord Commander calls for able hands to serve the realm. Read his notice on the board!

speaker: narrator
text: He lowers his bell and his voice with it.

speaker: town crier
text: If it's a sword arm they want of you, they'll send you to the training yard, to Sir Cedric. Sir Cedric, as was. Mind your manners with him; whatever folk say, he's a fair man.

speaker: narrator
text: A red-faced man in Greendale's colors, a brass bell in one hand and a scroll of notices in the other. You hear him across the square before you see him.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Main Square, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The merchant's flyer advertises quality goods from Master Merchant Aldric and would serve as a good introduction when visiting the Market District.

speaker: narrator
text: Castle Approach

speaker: narrator
text: A wide avenue lined with statues of Greendale's heroes leads to an impressive castle of white stone. Tall spires reach toward the sky, and colorful banners snap in the wind. Fewer guards than the posts were built for patrol the approach, and those who remain keep their voices low. The royal standard is gone from the highest spire.

speaker: herald
text: Greetings, traveler. I must examine your credentials before you pass into the courtyard. A sealed pass will do, or a letter. Forgive the quiet halls. Since King Alden vanished, half the court has gone home to wait for news.

speaker: castle guard captain
text: Welcome to the castle grounds. Sir Cedric is in the courtyard. He holds no rank now, but we still call him Sir, most of us, and you'll do the same if you've any sense. He's looking for people who can hold their own. If that's why you're here, he'll want to see you with a blade.

speaker: narrator
text: He lowers his voice.

speaker: castle guard captain
text: And a word of advice: ask no questions about the king. His Majesty has not been seen these three weeks, since the night he vanished from his own chambers. The word sent out to the villages is that he is ill. The Lord Commander rules in his name until he returns.

speaker: narrator
text: A thin man in a tabard of the royal arms, a ledger open on a stand beside him. He looks hard at every seal and not at much else.

speaker: narrator
text: A grey-moustached officer in polished armor, standing where he can see both the gate and the courtyard arch. He keeps his voice low out of habit.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Castle Approach, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The herald examines the seal carefully and nods with approval.

speaker: herald
text: A sound seal. You may pass into the courtyard.

speaker: narrator
text: He does not look at the line above the seal, where the name has been scraped away. He writes something in his ledger.

speaker: herald
text: Your credentials have been verified. The courtyard is through the west arch; you will find Sir Cedric there.

speaker: narrator
text: Castle Courtyard

speaker: narrator
text: An expansive courtyard within the castle walls, featuring training grounds where knights practice their swordwork. Ancient oak trees provide shade for stone benches, and a stable houses magnificent warhorses, though half its stalls stand empty since the king's own guard rode out to search for him. The castle's main hall rises before you, its great doors carved with the symbols of Greendale's noble houses.

speaker: narrator
text: You draw the training sword. Before you can take your stance, Sir Cedric catches your wrist and turns the blade to the light.

speaker: sir cedric
text: That notch by the guard. I put it there at fourteen, swinging at a post I'd been told to leave alone. Where did you get this?

speaker: narrator
text: You tell him about the old man by the fire on the mountain path, and what he asked you to say.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric is silent for a long moment. When he speaks, his voice is low.

speaker: sir cedric
text: The sergeant never believed in anything he couldn't hit. That he believes in me...

speaker: narrator
text: He lets go of your wrist and steps back.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Show me what he taught you, then.

speaker: narrator
text: He takes a practice blade from the rack and squares off against you.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Three forms, the way he drilled them. When I come at you, answer me: strike, guard or turn. Say it as you do it.

speaker: narrator
text: (Answer him with: say strike, say guard or say turn to Sir Cedric.)

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric raises his blade high over his left shoulder.

speaker: sir cedric
text: High cut!

speaker: sir cedric
text: Greetings, traveler. I am Cedric. Some here still call me Sir; you need not. The Lord Commander's notice asks for able hands; I ask for mine here in the yard, where I can see what they can do. There is a storm gathering over this—

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric stops mid-sentence. His eyes have fallen on the ancient amulet at your chest.

speaker: sir cedric
text: That sigil. The sun rising over three linked rings. I have seen it only in the old histories in the castle archive: it is the mark of the Wardens of the Dawn. They guarded this kingdom long ago, and most have forgotten them. The oldest histories draw the mark another way: a tree under two moons, from before there were three things to guard. Whoever wore that amulet before you was a Warden, and your family is bound to them. I know no more than that. But I know enough to listen to you. There is a storm gathering over this kingdom, and I do not yet know its name. The sigil tells me where you come from; it does not tell me what you can do. Show me, with a blade, here in the yard.

speaker: training master
text: A visitor. Keep off the sand while they're drilling.

speaker: narrator
text: He glances toward Sir Cedric and away again.

speaker: training master
text: Sir Cedric held the watch on the king's wall the night His Majesty vanished, and the next morning two men of the night watch swore he had left his post. They took his knighthood for it. I have known Cedric twenty years. He has never left a post in his life. The watch's story was too neat.

speaker: narrator
text: He leans closer, lowering his voice.

speaker: training master
text: There's talk of papers somewhere that tell a different story. I'm too old and too watched to go looking. You're neither.

speaker: narrator
text: The squires keep their eyes on their drill. One of them answers without turning.

speaker: squires
text: Can't stop. The Training Master's watching, and he counts.

speaker: narrator
text: A tall knight in old, dented mail. A pale patch on his surcoat shows where his device has been unpicked, and the scabbard at his hip hangs empty. He stands as if he were still on watch.

speaker: narrator
text: A grey-haired knight with a voice worn rough from shouting across the yard. His armour is old and dented and polished anyway. He watches the squires' feet, not their swords.

speaker: narrator
text: A dozen squires at drill in the yard, wooden swords knocking. Between passes they glance at Sir Cedric and whisper.

speaker: narrator
text: You don't find anything of particular interest around the benches. The squires are watching you curiously — perhaps you should talk to them first to learn more about this place.

text: New side quest

text: The Knight's Test

text: Sir Cedric wants to see proof of your combat abilities before trusting you with important responsibilities. Demonstrate your martial skills with a training sword.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric knew the sigil on your amulet: the sun rising over three linked rings, the mark of the Wardens of the Dawn. Whoever wore it before you was a Warden, he says, and your family is bound to them.

speaker: narrator
text: A mysterious amulet inscribed with runes. At its centre is the sigil of the Wardens of the Dawn: the sun rising over three linked rings. It is faintly warm in your hand.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Not yet. Show me what you can do with a blade first; then we will talk of the rest.

text: The Gathering Storm: Sir Cedric knew the sigil on your amulet: the sun rising over three linked rings, the mark of the Wardens of the Dawn. Whoever wore it before you was a Warden, he says, and your family is bound to them.

text: The Knight's Test: Sir Cedric wants to see proof of your combat abilities before trusting you with important responsibilities. Demonstrate your martial skills with a training sword.

text: He raises his blade high over his left shoulder.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Talk after.

speaker: narrator
text: You bring the training sword up and his blade rings off it.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Guard. Good.

text: He steps back, then drives straight at your middle.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Lunge!

speaker: narrator
text: He drives straight at your middle.

text: You step aside and his point slides past your ribs.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Turn. He taught you that much.

text: Well?

text: He swings wide and leaves his chest open.

text: You tap his chest with the flat of the blade.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric lowers his blade and nods.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Three for three. I can trust a hand like that at my back.

speaker: narrator
text: He pauses, and his voice drops.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Now I can tell you the rest. Whatever is wrong in this kingdom, a sword will not find it.

speaker: sir cedric
text: The old tales speak of a sprite called Nyx, deep in the Enchanted Forest. She knows things no archive does. If anyone can tell us what we are facing, it is her.

speaker: sir cedric
text: The forest does not forgive the unprepared. The Market District sells what you will want: a forest survival kit, an enhanced lantern and quality rope. Get all three before you go.

speaker: narrator
text: He straightens.

speaker: sir cedric
text: And see me before you go to the market, Elior. I will not send you there with empty pockets.

text: Sir Cedric mentioned the need for proper equipment for forest expeditions. Gather essential supplies from the Market District.

text: You have successfully demonstrated your combat skills to Sir Cedric. He now trusts your abilities!

text: You held your own in the yard. Few do, against me.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric reaches into his pouch and hands you a bag of coins.

speaker: sir cedric
text: For the market. The kit, the lantern and the rope; it will cover all three, if you do not let the merchants see how badly you want them.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric hesitates, then rests a hand on a small pouch at his belt.

speaker: sir cedric
text: One more thing, since the forest is where you are bound. My family has kept a charm for generations: nature's charm, carved for the knights who first made pacts with the forest spirits. Prove yourself in more than a sparring yard, and we will speak of it again.

text: How goes your preparation? Whatever is coming does not wait on us. Neither should you.

text: Welcome to the castle grounds. Sir Cedric is in the courtyard. He holds no rank now, but we still call him Sir, most of us, and you'll do the same if you've any sense. I hear you held your own against him. Not many do.

speaker: narrator
text: Market District

speaker: narrator
text: Narrow streets crammed with shops and trading posts weave a maze of commerce. Spices, leather, and fresh bread scent the air. Merchant wagons clog passageways while deals are argued in several languages. Serious business gets done here.

speaker: narrator
text: Master Merchant Aldric looks at your boots, then at your face.

speaker: master merchant aldric
text: I deal only with established customers. A new face brings me an introduction. Even one of my own handbills will do.

speaker: caravan master thorne
text: You've the look of someone who isn't afraid of trees. My caravan to Heavensforth never came through: spice, cloth, and my people with it, lost somewhere in the Enchanted Forest. Goods I can write off. People I can't. Would you be willing to search for them? I'd be forever in your debt.

speaker: caravan master thorne
text: Our road to Heavensforth runs along the forest's edge. It was safe enough a month ago, while the king's riders patrolled it. Nobody patrols it since the king went; every rider the castle has is out looking for him.

speaker: caravan master thorne
text: Brenn, my guard, came stumbling back alone two nights ago. Says the ravine path gave way and he ran. Ran! He's skulking in the warehouse now. I'll deal with him once my people are home.

speaker: narrator
text: A broad man in a good coat, standing among coils of rope and racks of lanterns. He looks at your boots before he looks at your face.

speaker: narrator
text: A weather-beaten caravan master with a ledger under his arm and road dust in the creases of his coat.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Market District, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

text: One of mine. Then someone thought you worth sending. This flyer grants you access to our premium selection. Have a look.

text: A comprehensive kit containing everything needed for safe forest exploration: dried food, water purification tablets, protective gear, a compass, and magical wards against forest spirits.

text: A magically enhanced lantern that burns with bright, steady light. The enchantment allows it to illuminate hidden paths and reveal magical auras that would otherwise remain invisible.

text: Welcome to Aldric's. Rope that holds, lanterns that stay lit, and nothing that comes apart on the road. My premium selection includes: - Forest Survival Kit: 50 gold coins - Enhanced Lantern: 40 gold coins - Quality Rope: 20 gold coins

text: The Merchant's Lost Caravan

speaker: narrator
text: Caravan Master Thorne's valuable caravan has gone missing in the Enchanted Forest. Find out what happened to the merchants and their goods.

speaker: brenn
text: If you've come from Thorne, you'll have heard. The path just went, out from under the wagons. I was hanging over the ravine by one hand. When I got up I ran for help, I swear I did. But the forest turned me round, and I couldn't find the road again for two days. So I came back. Somebody had to tell him.

speaker: caravan master thorne
text: Any word? … No. I've stopped counting the goods. I count the days.

speaker: narrator
text: The Merchant's Lost Caravan: Caravan Master Thorne's valuable caravan has gone missing in the Enchanted Forest. Find out what happened to the merchants and their goods.

text: The Silver Stag Inn

speaker: narrator
text: A three-story inn glows with warm yellow light. Conversations from travelers and locals merge into a comforting din while tales are traded over bread and ale. Stag mounts and adventuring trophies line the walls. The place feels welcoming; information flows here as freely as the drink.

speaker: narrator
text: A brass key to a private room at The Silver Stag Inn. The room provides a quiet space for studying and safe storage of important items.

speaker: narrator
text: The door is made of sturdy oak wood with decorative iron hinges and a simple latch. The door frame is carved with intricate patterns typical of the inn's welcoming atmosphere. This door provides access to the upper floor where guests can rent private rooms for rest and storage.

speaker: innkeeper marcus
text: Welcome to The Silver Stag. Hot stew, clean sheets, and a door that locks. I can offer you: - Room Key: 10 gold coins

speaker: innkeeper marcus
text: My girl, Elena. She's been poorly three weeks. … Talk to her, if you've a kind word to spare. She'll tell it better than I can.

speaker: narrator
text: Elena coughs, and turns it into a smile.

speaker: barmaid elena
text: Sorry. I'm slow today. I'm slow every day now. It's a curse, the healers say. It came on me in the night, three weeks back, and every morning I wake a little colder. Father asks anyone who comes in with a staff. I think he's run out of people to ask.

speaker: narrator
text: A big man in a stained apron who runs The Silver Stag Inn. He talks to every guest and watches only one: his daughter, across the room.

speaker: narrator
text: A young woman who moves slowly, as if every tray weighs twice what it should. Her lips are grey, and the cup she sets down rattles.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Silver Stag Inn, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

text: You've spoken with Elena. Then you've seen. She says she's only tired. … If you can help her, name it, and this house will find it.

speaker: innkeeper marcus
text: It came on her the week the king went. The whole town was out in the streets asking after him, and I was upstairs with a cold cloth.

speaker: narrator
text: Elena pulls her shawl tighter.

speaker: barmaid elena

text: The Innkeeper's Daughter: Elena, the barmaid at the Silver Stag, wakes a little colder every morning. The healers call it a curse; nobody can say who laid it.

text: That room upstairs? Its last lodger was a man in a grey cloak. Never gave a name, wrote half the night by candle, and was gone one morning without paying. It was the week the king went. I've aired it since. You'll find it clean.

speaker: forest sprites
text: Nymphs are east—

speaker: forest sprites
text: —with their riddles.

speaker: narrator
text: The Forest Guardian's Riddles: The forest sprites have challenged you to prove your wisdom by solving the riddles of the forest guardians. You must journey east from the Forest Entrance to the Whispering Glade, where ancient spirits will test your understanding of forest ways and natural wisdom.

speaker: narrator
text: Ancient Grove

speaker: narrator
text: A circular clearing dominated by trees so old and massive they seem to touch the sky. Their bark bears carved symbols that predate human memory, and the air shimmers with concentrated magic. At the center grows a tree unlike any other - its silver bark gleams and its leaves whisper secrets in an ancient tongue. This is clearly a place of power and the sacred gateway to the forest's deepest mysteries.

speaker: narrator
text: The tree stands taller than anything around it. Its bark is silver, smooth as metal and warm under your hand. You stand there long enough, and something in the wood turns over, like a sleeper waking. The ancient tree spirit is awake.

speaker: narrator
text: The enchanted acorn pulses with magical energy in response to the sacred grove, warm as a held hand, and turns in your palm toward the silver-barked tree.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Ancient Grove, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The silver bark is warm under your hand. Somewhere in it, the spirit is listening.

speaker: narrator
text: A face gathers in the knots of the silver bark and turns toward you.

speaker: ancient tree spirit
text: You walk like spring. Everything new, nothing kept.

speaker: ancient tree spirit
text: I don't teach for nothing. Bring me something that hasn't grown yet.

speaker: narrator
text: The spirit lives in the silver-barked tree. Its face is only there when you stop looking for it: two knots for eyes, a split in the bark for a mouth. Moss grows on it in rings, one for every winter. The bark is warm under your hand, and below your feet the roots shift slowly, like someone turning over in their sleep.

speaker: narrator
text: The bark around the knots softens.

speaker: ancient tree spirit
text: Next spring's tree, and you carried it here instead of planting it. Good. Listen, then.

speaker: narrator
text: The voices of the grove settle into you: the creak of branches, the talk of roots, the small sounds in the undergrowth. You can understand them now.

speaker: narrator
text: You have learned Forest Speech.

speaker: ancient tree spirit
text: You can hear them now. The grove is uneasy. The nymphs in the glade east of the entrance have something for these roots. Answer them, and bring back what they give you.

speaker: narrator
text: Whispers in the Wind

speaker: narrator
text: The Ancient Tree Spirit has sensed mystical beings hidden within the forest's depths. Gentle whispers carry on the wind, speaking of ancient wisdom and forgotten lore. To prove yourself worthy of the forest's trust, you must seek out these hidden spirits in the Whispering Glade and demonstrate your understanding of nature's mysteries.

speaker: narrator
text: Delicate leaves that shimmer with a soft argent sheen even in shadow. Their surfaces refract light into faint auroral threads, and a cool, clean scent clings to them. Holding them you sense tranquil, ancient vitality. A healer would know what to do with these.

speaker: ancient tree spirit
text: Still summer for you, then — all errands.

speaker: ancient tree spirit
text: The nymphs in the glade east of the entrance have something for these roots. Answer them, and bring back what they give you.

speaker: narrator
text: Whispers in the Wind: The Ancient Tree Spirit has sensed mystical beings hidden within the forest's depths. Gentle whispers carry on the wind, speaking of ancient wisdom and forgotten lore. To prove yourself worthy of the forest's trust, you must seek out these hidden spirits in the Whispering Glade and demonstrate your understanding of nature's mysteries.

speaker: narrator
text: Whispering Glade

speaker: narrator
text: A peaceful meadow opens around a small stream that babbles over smooth stones. Wildflowers blanket the ground and butterflies drift through warm sunlight. The water's murmur soothes, yet faint voices ride the breeze — whispers hinting at ancient secrets. Near the crystal stream you sense watchful, unseen guardians.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Whispering Glade, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: You hold still and let the glade come to you. The stream is not only water: there are shapes sitting in it, and they have been watching you all along. The water nymphs let you see them.

speaker: narrator
text: The stream rises into shapes.

speaker: water nymphs
text: Came all this way to stand in our water? Will you answer three questions, then? Shall we start?

speaker: water nymphs
text: I am the forest's blood that flows without wound, the sky's gift that falls without being thrown. I give life yet can take it, am soft yet can carve stone. What am I?

speaker: narrator
text: (Answer them with: say <your answer> to water nymphs.)

speaker: narrator
text: Three of them, or four; it is hard to count water. They sit waist-deep in the stream, and the stream runs through them. When you lean closer, every one of them leans closer too.

speaker: narrator
text: The stream runs a little faster round your boots. The water nymphs nod.

speaker: water nymphs
text: Did you know it, or guess it? Does it matter? What about this one?

speaker: water nymphs
text: I smile, yet I have no eyes. I have a face, yet it is not my own. Put me on and I hide you; leave me behind and I tell whose work it was. What am I?

speaker: water nymphs
text: Back so soon? Do you remember where we were? The second one, wasn't it?

speaker: narrator
text: For a moment every one of the water nymphs wears your face. Then they nod.

speaker: water nymphs
text: Purpose follows me, and power follows purpose. A lie may wear my coat, but it cannot keep it on. I am hard to say and harder to hear, and I grow no lighter for being hidden. What am I?

speaker: water nymphs
text: Back so soon? Do you remember where we were? The third one, wasn't it?

speaker: narrator
text: The water nymphs laugh, a sound like water over a weir.

speaker: water nymphs
text: Three for three — who taught you to listen like that? Will you take what grows here? Who else would we give it to?

speaker: narrator
text: They draw back from the bank. The crystal-clear water and the moonflowers at its edge are there for the taking.

speaker: narrator
text: You have successfully solved the riddles of the forest guardians, proving your wisdom and respect for the natural world. The forest spirits acknowledge your understanding.

speaker: narrator
text: Water from the sacred spring in the Whispering Glade, this liquid is so pure it seems to glow with its own inner light. The water has been blessed by the water nymphs and carries powerful purification magic that can break curses and cleanse dark enchantments. Each drop sparkles like liquid starlight, and the container feels cool to the touch. The liquid moves with an otherworldly fluidity, and you can sense the powerful purification magic contained within. This water could break even the strongest curses.

speaker: narrator
text: Ethereal white flowers that bloom only in places where moonlight and magic converge. Their petals shimmer with a silvery luminescence and give off a faint, sweet fragrance that seems to calm the mind and spirit. These rare blossoms are prized by herbalists and magical practitioners for their ability to enhance divination and provide protection against nightmares and dark visions. As you watch, the petals seem to move gently even though there's no breeze, and you notice tiny motes of silvery light drifting from the blooms like magical pollen.

speaker: water nymphs
text: Back again? Wasn't three enough? What more could we ask you?

speaker: water nymphs
text: Have you seen the streams come down thinner from the hills this season? What drinks up there before we do, that the fields below the city taste it first?

speaker: narrator
text: The moonflowers seem to approve of your gentle touch, their silvery glow pulsing warmly as you gather them. These blessed blooms will aid in healing and protection magic.

speaker: narrator
text: The moonflowers remain dormant here. They likely have special significance for healing or magical purposes.

speaker: narrator
text: The moonflowers glow more brightly in the magical atmosphere of the forest, their protective properties enhanced.

speaker: narrator
text: You pour some of the crystal-clear water at the foot of the silver tree and set the moonflowers in the wet soil. They take root at once and begin to glow.

speaker: ancient tree spirit
text: Rain and a night's flowers. That will see the roots through winter.

speaker: narrator
text: South of the grove, branches pull apart with a long creak.

speaker: ancient tree spirit
text: Nyx lives at the end of that path. She doesn't come for asking — read her altar before you call her.

speaker: narrator
text: You have communed with the Water Nymphs in the Whispering Glade, solved their ancient riddles, and earned their sacred gifts. By returning these blessed items to the Ancient Tree Spirit, you have proven yourself a true friend to the woodland spirits and earned the forest's trust.

speaker: ancient tree spirit
text: Autumn, for you. You came with nothing and you leave carrying things. The way south is yours.

speaker: narrator
text: The woodland creatures gather around you excitedly. A family of squirrels chatters frantically about strange noises from the deep ravine to the northeast. An old owl hoots solemnly about 'metal beasts trapped in the earth-scar where the stone walls weep.' The animals describe a steep ravine hidden beyond the thickest part of the forest, where something seems to be moving. The owl looks at you, and then at the ravine.

speaker: narrator
text: Looking down into the ravine, you can see the remnants of a merchant caravan trapped at the bottom. The wooden wagon wheels are visible among the rocks, and you can hear faint voices calling for help. The walls are steep and dangerous - you'll need rope or other climbing equipment to safely reach the bottom and see what is there.

speaker: narrator
text: You secure one end of your quality rope to a sturdy tree and lower it into the ravine. Rappelling down carefully, you find the trapped merchant caravan at the bottom. The merchants are injured but alive, and their wagon is damaged but some goods are salvageable. Working together, you create a rope system that allows everyone to climb to safety. The grateful merchants gather their most valuable goods and follow you back to civilization. The caravan has been successfully rescued!

speaker: narrator
text: Golden light settles on split lips and wrenched ankles, and one by one the merchants stop wincing.

speaker: narrator
text: A spice trader flexes a hand she has been cradling since the ravine.

speaker: spice trader
text: Three days down there and I'd stopped feeling these fingers. Tell Thorne he owes you twice now.

speaker: caravan master thorne
text: You found them. All of them. … I owe you more than I can pay, so take these instead. My wagon-master says a frightened man in Heavensforth paid him to carry them to Greendale, and begged him to put them in no hands but a knight's. I believe they could clear a good man's name.

speaker: narrator
text: Thorne hands you a stack of secret documents.

speaker: caravan master thorne
text: And my people tell me you didn't just haul them out of that hole — you mended them where they sat. One of the spice traders says her hand's never been better. I don't know how a man repays a debt twice over.

speaker: narrator
text: You successfully located the missing caravan trapped in a deep ravine within the Enchanted Forest. Using your forest magic, you discovered their location, then employed quality rope to rappel down and rescue the trapped merchants. All merchants survived the ordeal, and Caravan Master Thorne rewarded you with secret documents containing evidence that can clear Sir Cedric's name of false accusations from a past court case.

speaker: narrator
text: The merchant caravan is in rough shape but the people are safe. The wagon's wheels are cracked and the canvas cover is torn, but the structure is sound. Several merchants tend to minor injuries while sorting through their goods. You see spice containers, bolts of fine cloth, and various trade items. The merchants look at you with deep gratitude—you clearly saved their lives.

speaker: brenn
text: They're home? All of them? … Thank you. Thorne says I'm to have my wages and not a copper more. I suppose that's fair. I ran. Unless somebody told him what it was like out there. He'd never hear it from me.

speaker: narrator
text: You speak for Brenn: the path gave way under him too, and fear is not the same as cowardice. He came back to tell you, when he could have kept running.

speaker: caravan master thorne
text: … He did come back, didn't he. … All right. One more road. If he runs again, he walks home.

speaker: brenn
text: Thorne says one more road. He says somebody spoke for me. … I won't run again. Not this time.

speaker: narrator
text: A sworn confession and a letter closed with black wax. They speak of gold, a gate and a night, but without knowing whose night, you cannot make sense of them.

speaker: caravan master thorne
text: My people are home, and I still wake up counting them. Those papers I gave you: I hope they find the knight they were meant for.

speaker: caravan master thorne
text: Which leaves Brenn. A guard who runs is no guard. He's sitting in the warehouse waiting for his wages, and wages are all he'll get from me.

speaker: narrator
text: Golden light goes into Elena from your hands. She gasps as colour comes back to her cheeks, and she stands a little straighter.

speaker: narrator
text: The healing has made her stronger, but the curse still clings to her.

speaker: narrator
text: As the golden light fades, something surfaces on the inside of Elena's wrist: a small silver mark in the shape of a mask, smooth and smiling, with no eyes behind it. The curse is wearing a face. You have never seen its like, and you cannot say whose it is.

speaker: narrator
text: Elena sees you looking at her wrist and tugs her sleeve down over the silver mark.

speaker: barmaid elena
text: It came the same night as the curse. Since then I dream of a smiling face with no eyes, and it never says a true word.

speaker: narrator
text: Elena turns her hand over and looks at it as if it belonged to someone else.

speaker: barmaid elena
text: It didn't take. I felt it go in, warm as a hearth, and then the cold closed over it again.

speaker: barmaid elena
text: Master Lyria sat with me once, when it began. If anyone knows what comes next, she does.

speaker: narrator
text: A young woman with a little colour back in her face. She still moves carefully, like someone waiting for the cold to come back. On the inside of her wrist, a small silver mask shows through her skin.

speaker: narrator
text: The water runs over Elena's wrist and down her fingers, and where it runs the grey goes out of her skin. She gasps, then breathes easier than she has in weeks.

speaker: narrator
text: Elena stands straighter. The curse's hold on her has been greatly weakened by the purification.

speaker: narrator
text: Elena rubs at the inside of her wrist.

speaker: barmaid elena
text: The water stung, and then it was gone, and some of the cold went with it. But it is still holding on. I can feel it, here.

speaker: narrator
text: A young woman, steadier now, with the grey gone from her skin. She keeps rubbing the inside of her wrist. The silver mask on her wrist is untouched by the water.

speaker: narrator
text: The unbinding takes hold, and Elena cries out, once. Then she straightens, and breathes, and looks at her hands as if she had only now got them back.

speaker: narrator
text: On her wrist the silver mask goes on smiling a moment longer, then fades like breath on a cold window, and is gone.

speaker: narrator
text: You made Elena strong with greater heal, washed the mark in water from the nymphs' spring, and unbound the curse with the Wardens' dispel. The silver mask on her wrist faded, and she is warm again.

speaker: narrator
text: Marcus has to wipe his eyes before he can speak.

speaker: innkeeper marcus
text: You gave me back my girl. … This druidic charm has hung over our door longer than there's been a Silver Stag. My grandmother said it came out of the forest, and the forest would know it again. Take it. It kept this house. Let it keep you.

speaker: narrator
text: He presses the carved wood into your hands. You receive a druidic charm.

speaker: narrator
text: Elena sets her tray down and takes both your hands.

speaker: barmaid elena
text: Oh, thank you so much! I'm warm. I'd forgotten what that was like. Father says the charm over our door is yours now, and he won't hear a word against it.

speaker: narrator
text: Elena, quick on her feet again, with a tray on each arm. When she catches your eye she lifts one to you, like a toast.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell Marcus about the silver mask on Elena's wrist: the curse was no ill wind. Someone set it on her on purpose.

speaker: innkeeper marcus
text: On purpose. … Someone chose my girl. … Then this house sleeps with one eye open from now on. Thank you for telling me. I'd sooner know it than be comforted by a lie.

speaker: narrator
text: An ancient charm carved from sacred oak and blessed by generations of druids. The wooden pendant is etched with mystical symbols that seem to pulse with natural magic. Wrapped in silver wire and suspended from a leather cord, it emanates a warm, protective energy. This sacred charm represents the bond between nature and civilization. The intricate carvings depict intertwined branches and leaves, symbols of the eternal cycle of growth and renewal. You can feel the gratitude and love that Marcus poured into this gift when he gave it to you for saving his daughter Elena from the dark curse.

speaker: narrator
text: The druidic charm glows faintly with natural magic. It feels especially potent here, but you sense it has a greater purpose that requires the right location and companions.

speaker: innkeeper marcus
text: My daughter is healthy and happy again. Hear her? Singing over the trays. Your room's free here as long as this house stands.

speaker: innkeeper marcus
text: An ill wind, that's all it was. Bad luck, blown in off the road, settling on the one soul in this house who never harmed anyone.

speaker: narrator
text: Cedric's Lost Honor

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric was stripped of his knighthood after the night King Alden vanished: two men of the night watch swore he had left his post. Investigate what happened that night and find evidence to clear his name.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric's jaw tightens.

speaker: sir cedric
text: You will have heard what they say of me. I held the king's wall the night he vanished, and he was lost on my watch. Whatever else is true, that is. I will not make excuses.

speaker: narrator
text: The Training Master nods.

speaker: training master
text: Still at it? Good. Ask the squires. Boys and girls in a barracks hear things an old knight never does.

speaker: narrator
text: The young squires lower their voices and glance around nervously.

speaker: squires
text: We're not supposed to talk about it, but we've heard the older knights whispering about Sir Cedric's disgrace. They say he left the king's wall the night His Majesty vanished, and that whoever took the king walked in through the gap.

speaker: narrator
text: One squire looks particularly troubled.

speaker: squires
text: But it doesn't make sense. Sir Cedric made us stand a post in the rain till our boots filled. He would never leave one.

speaker: narrator
text: Another squire nods.

speaker: squires
text: A squire before us kept a diary that week. It's under the stone benches. Read it; it says what we can't.

speaker: narrator
text: Cedric's Lost Honor: Sir Cedric was stripped of his knighthood after the night King Alden vanished: two men of the night watch swore he had left his post. Investigate what happened that night and find evidence to clear his name.

speaker: narrator
text: Remembering what the squires told you, you look more carefully under one of the ancient stone benches and discover a worn leather diary that appears to have been left by a former squire.

speaker: narrator
text: You found a squire's diary!

speaker: narrator
text: A worn leather-bound diary belonging to a former squire. The pages are filled with observations about castle life and training exercises. There are also notes about Sir Cedric's supposed disgrace and the night the king vanished. The handwriting is careful and deliberate. Several entries focus on Sir Cedric's disgrace and the missing evidence that could clear his name.

speaker: narrator
text: The entries in the squire's diary reveal a troubling story...

speaker: narrator
text: The morning after the king vanished:

speaker: squires
text: 'They have taken Sir Cedric's sword. Two men of the night watch swear he left the king's wall at the third bell. I was on the yard steps until midnight, and he never moved.'

speaker: narrator
text: Some days later:

speaker: squires
text: 'One of those two watchmen is gone. He packed in the night and took the road to Heavensforth, they say. A man with a clear conscience does not run.'

speaker: narrator
text: Last entry:

speaker: squires
text: 'A carter swears the watchman sent something back from Heavensforth, papers, with a merchant caravan bound for Greendale. The caravan never came; they say it was lost on the forest road. If those papers are still out there, they could clear Sir Cedric's name.'

speaker: narrator
text: The diary points to papers sent from Heavensforth by a watchman who fled, on a caravan that never arrived. The lost caravan's papers might still be out there…

speaker: narrator
text: After reading the diary, you place it back where you found it. This keeps the information safe while you no longer carry the diary.

speaker: narrator
text: According to the squires and their diary, one of the watchmen who accused Cedric fled to Heavensforth and sent papers back with a merchant caravan that never arrived. Find these papers to restore his honor.

speaker: narrator
text: A confession from a man of the night watch, written in Heavensforth where he fled. He swears that he and another were paid to leave the king's postern gate unguarded on the night King Alden vanished, and to say afterwards that Sir Cedric had left his post. Pinned to it is the letter that paid them, closed with black wax pressed with a twisted rune, the same kind of rune as the token you fished out of Willowbrook's well. It names where the king was to be carried: the bastion on the shattered ridge, north of the hills. It ends with a name in an old script you cannot read.

speaker: narrator
text: Cedric's Lost Honor: According to the squires and their diary, one of the watchmen who accused Cedric fled to Heavensforth and sent papers back with a merchant caravan that never arrived. Find these papers to restore his honor.

speaker: narrator
text: You have found the papers: a watchman's confession that he and another were paid to leave the king's postern unguarded and to blame Sir Cedric, with the letter that paid them, sealed with a twisted rune. Present them to the Lord Commander in the Great Hall to restore his honor.

speaker: narrator
text: The Lord Commander looks at you with interest.

speaker: lord commander
text: I am told you carry papers touching on Sir Cedric's case, and on the night His Majesty vanished. If they bear on either, give them to me.

speaker: narrator
text: Cedric's Lost Honor: You have found the papers: a watchman's confession that he and another were paid to leave the king's postern unguarded and to blame Sir Cedric, with the letter that paid them, sealed with a twisted rune. Present them to the Lord Commander in the Great Hall to restore his honor.

speaker: narrator
text: The Lord Commander reads the confession, then the letter. At its last line his face goes grey.

speaker: lord commander
text: This is the old court script. It reads: By the will of Malakar.

speaker: narrator
text: He lowers the page.

speaker: lord commander
text: Malakar is a name from children's tales. Yet someone paid gold in it, and on that night of all nights. Sir Cedric did not leave his post. He was chosen to carry the blame. I hereby restore his knighthood and strike the charge from the record.

speaker: narrator
text: He beckons a page and speaks a few quiet words. The boy runs off toward the armoury, and returns carrying a long bundle wrapped in oilcloth.

speaker: lord commander
text: Take this to the training yard. A knight should not stand among his squires with an empty scabbard.

speaker: narrator
text: The papers from Thorne's caravan cleared Sir Cedric's name. The watch was paid to let the king be taken, by the will of Malakar, and he was carried to the bastion on the shattered ridge.

speaker: narrator
text: You have cleared Sir Cedric's name. The night watch was paid to leave the king's postern open and to blame him, and the letter that paid them was written in Malakar's name.

speaker: narrator
text: The Lord Commander nods with satisfaction.

speaker: lord commander
text: Sir Cedric's knighthood is restored and the charge struck from the record. As for the name in that letter, I have sent riders to Heavensforth for the watchman who confessed. Whoever paid in that name will be found.

speaker: narrator
text: The Gathering Storm: The papers from Thorne's caravan cleared Sir Cedric's name. The watch was paid to let the king be taken, by the will of Malakar, and he was carried to the bastion on the shattered ridge.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric's sword hangs at his hip again. He rests a hand on its hilt as you approach, as if to be sure it is real.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Elior. You have cleared my name. And more than that: the king was not lost on my watch. He was taken, by men who were paid to let it happen.

speaker: narrator
text: He is quiet for a moment.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Malakar. My grandmother frightened me with that name when I was small. Whoever hides behind it took my king, and the papers say where: the bastion on the shattered ridge. I mean to find him.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric reaches into his pack and takes out a small wooden charm, dark with handling.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Do you remember what I told you in the yard? That I would not give an heirloom of my house to someone I had known a day. I have known you long enough now. Take nature's charm. It was carved for the knights who first made pacts with the forest spirits, and it is one of the three that call Nyx. You will need it more than I will.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive nature's charm.

speaker: narrator
text: The Training Master nods respectfully.

speaker: training master
text: You've seen it, then? His sword at his hip again. I stood in this yard the morning they took it from him, and I held my tongue. I'll not make that mistake twice. Greendale owes you, and so do I.

speaker: narrator
text: The squires have abandoned their drill and crowd together, grinning.

speaker: squires
text: Did you see? They gave Sir Cedric his sword back! He walked into the yard this morning with it at his hip, and the Training Master saluted him in front of everyone.

speaker: narrator
text: One squire looks at you shyly.

speaker: squires
text: He said it was you who found the papers. Thank you.

speaker: narrator
text: A tall knight in old, dented mail. His sword hangs at his hip once more, and he carries himself like a man who has been given back his name.

speaker: narrator
text: An ancient charm blessed by the knights of old, carved from living wood and inlaid with silver runes. It pulses with a gentle green light and seems to resonate with the natural world. This is clearly one of the sacred charms mentioned in the old texts - those needed to summon the forest sprite Nyx.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Thanks to you, my knighthood is restored and the charge struck from my record. Now I can turn to what matters: the king, and whoever wears that old name.

speaker: narrator
text: Lyria turns one leaf toward the window, and for a moment she forgets to breathe.

speaker: lyria
text: Silverbark. From the old tree itself, not a cutting. I have only ever read of these.

speaker: narrator
text: She lays them in a shallow dish as if they might bruise.

speaker: lyria
text: Steeped, a single leaf breaks a fever in a night. Greendale will have a gentler winter because of you, Elior.

speaker: narrator
text: The dish of silver leaves sits on the windowsill where the light can reach it.

speaker: castle guard captain
text: Welcome to the castle grounds. Sir Cedric is in the courtyard. Sir by right again, and I'm glad to say it. I hear you held your own against him. Not many do.

speaker: narrator
text: He rings his bell twice, with relish.

speaker: town crier
text: And fresh news from the Great Hall! The Lord Commander has cleared Sir Cedric's name and given him back his sword. Sir Cedric, and no 'as was' about it!

speaker: narrator
text: Heart of the Forest

speaker: narrator
text: The deepest part of the Enchanted Forest, where reality feels fluid and magic flows like water. Impossible colors paint the landscape and the air sparkles with latent energy. A colossal tree dominates the center, its branches seeming to uphold the sky. Before it rests an ancient altar carved from starstone, runes pulsing with otherworldly light. This is Nyx's domain where profound secrets surface. The sacred grove path is the only passage into this mystical heart.

speaker: narrator
text: An ancient altar carved from a single piece of starstone, its surface adorned with mystical runes that pulse with otherworldly light. Three circular indentations suggest that specific items are meant to be placed here in a sacred ritual. The altar radiates powerful magic and seems to be waiting for the proper offerings to activate its full potential.

speaker: narrator
text: The druidic charm resonates with the mystical energy of this sacred place. It should be placed on the offering altar along with other sacred items to perform powerful rituals.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Heart of the Forest, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The three charms sink into the starstone, and the runes light one after another. Above the altar the light gathers and stays, the height of a woman. Nyx has come.

speaker: narrator
text: The light over the altar folds into a woman no taller than you, barefoot, leaves caught in her hair. She looks at you the way you look at a road you have walked before.

speaker: nyx
text: Elior. My deer sat with you in the glade at Willowbrook, before any of this. It said you were still. Few are. You gave the tree your acorn instead of keeping it. You answered the nymphs without bargaining. You brought me the three charms. The forest saw the road you took. It will keep watching. That is enough.

speaker: narrator

text: You found her. It is in your face; you look like a man who has been shown something. Whatever she gave you to see, I would see it too. Show me here, and I will stand beside you for whatever comes of it.

speaker: narrator
text: You take the forest heart crystal from your pack and hold it out between you and Sir Cedric. The tiny lights inside it gather, brighten, and spill outward, and the vision rises out of the crystal for both of you to see:

speaker: narrator
text: Then the voice from your dream, the one that called your name on the night of the storm:

text: Elior… how you have grown. Do not be afraid of me.
